blocks.text: Condo buildings in Chilliwack Downtown
No SnapStats for Chilliwack. CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables.
Ivy Green — 45775 Spadina Avenue

55+ freehold strata condo building: 24 condos, 3 storeys, built 1994, plan LMS1336, self-managed, pets not allowed (strata-manager building record). Listings describe it as a "55+ age-restricted apartment" in Chilliwack Downtown, freehold strata, with in-suite laundry.
Spadina Regency — 45765 Spadina Avenue

55+ freehold strata condo building, concrete construction, built 1989; the building directory records a 26-unit development, pets allowed. Listings state "55+ building where rentals and pets are permitted," with secure underground parking, elevator, clubhouse, workshop and a guest suite; the rental line in any older directory text is in any case void since November 24, 2022.
Chilliwack Gardens — 45749 Spadina Avenue

Low-rise strata, Apartment/Condo sub-type, labelled Chilliwack Downtown in listings, described as "rental-friendly (no age restrictions), No Pets," professionally managed, with heat and hot water included in the strata fee per the listing checked. Year built — conflict IN SOURCES: one current listing states 1980; another states 1979. This is the trap on the Spadina corridor: same street as two genuine 55+ buildings, opposite rules.
The Willows — 45893 Chesterfield Avenue

Apartment form confirmed by listings and by the building record: Strata Plan BCS3330, sub-area Chilliwack Downtown, Apartment dwelling type, with secure underground parking and in-suite laundry in listing text. Year built — conflict IN SOURCES: the building record states 2009; several current listings state 2008.
Unnamed building — 9060 Birch Street
Apartment form confirmed by a current listing: sub-type Apartment, labelled Chilliwack Downtown, built 2009, one block from Five Corners per its listing text.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: Municipally, the same area is planned through Schedule B3, the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan, of the City's 2050 Official Community Plan, with Schedule D-6 the "Downtown" development permit area.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two short corridors — Spadina Avenue (three strata buildings in a row: 45749, 45765 and 45775) and the Birch Street / Chesterfield Avenue / Cheam Avenue pocket by Five Corners (9000 and 9060 Birch Street, The Willows on Chesterfield, Magnolia Manor named on Cheam).
Schools: Chilliwack is SD33. Catchments are address-based and no SD33 locator run for a downtown address is on record.

Transit: BC Transit's Chilliwack service-improvements notice (December 18, 2025, effective January 4, 2026) records added Sunday-evening service for Route 57 Broadway, Route 53 Fairfield and Route 51, and BC Transit lists Route 66 Fraser Valley Express as serving Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby with daily service.

Health care: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd, Chilliwack, is a Fraser Health community hospital providing primary, core secondary and some specialty services — it sits just west of the downtown condo corridors.

A fourth Spadina building is filed under a different sub-area. Spadina Place (45535 Spadina Ave) is labelled Chilliwack Proper West in current listings, and a house on the same street is also labelled Proper West in listing data — a buyer who searches by sub-area label alone will find the same street filed under two different pages.

Downtown's condo stock splits into two pockets, not one district. The Spadina trio is 1980s–1990s stock by the hospital precinct; the Birch/Chesterfield/Cheam pocket (9000 and 9060 Birch, The Willows, Magnolia Manor) is 2000s stock by Five Corners and District 1881. Fees, construction and warranty history differ by pocket, not by the "downtown" label.

Chilliwack Downtown is a CADREB market, not a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board one, and the plan wording for infill is only partly confirmed. A buyer valuing infill potential needs to check with the City.

The Willows and Chilliwack Gardens each carry a build-year conflict. The Willows: 2009 in the building record, 2008 in several listings. Chilliwack Gardens: 1980 in one listing, 1979 in another. Neither conflict is resolved here — the strata plan registration record settles each definitively.

items.t: Municipal plan frame: Schedule B3 of the 2050 OCP is the "Downtown Neighbourhood Plan" covering this area, and Schedule D-6 is the "Downtown" development permit area; the OCP's other Schedule D areas (D-1 Drinking Water Supply, D-2 Hillside Environment, D-3 Riparian Area, D-4 Farm Home Plate, D-5 Hillside Development, D-7 Mixed-Use Areas, D-8 Residential, D-9 Commercial, D-10 Industrial) apply per parcel.

Board identity: Chilliwack is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market, not a Fraser Valley or Greater Vancouver board market; CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables.
How people search for it: "Chilliwack Downtown homes for sale," "District 1881 condos," "downtown Chilliwack apartments," "Five Corners Chilliwack homes."

Downtown has two penalty dates, close together. Chilliwack's second 5% penalty lands August 4, 2026 — barely a month after the July 2 first penalty — not in September as in Surrey or October as in the rural regime.

faq.a: Yes — six form-known apartment-condo buildings: Ivy Green (45775 Spadina Ave, 24 units, 1994, 55+), Spadina Regency (45765 Spadina Ave, 26 units, 1989, 55+), Chilliwack Gardens (45749 Spadina Ave, no age restriction), The Willows (45893 Chesterfield Ave, BCS3330), and two unnamed buildings at 9000 and 9060 Birch Street. Magnolia Manor on Cheam Avenue is named in listing text only and is not counted.
faq.q: Are there any condos in Chilliwack Downtown?

faq.a: No. Chilliwack is not covered by SnapStats and CADREB publishes no sub-area statistics. Price from the property's own CADREB comparables.
faq.q: Is there an official median price for Chilliwack Downtown?

faq.a: The Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500 — specifically Schedule B3, the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan, with the Schedule D-6 Downtown development permit area applying in the core.

For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. Short-term rentals are different: a bylaw can still restrict them, and the City regulates short-term rental operations under its own bylaw. In a 55+ building the tenant must still meet the age bylaw or an exemption.
faq.q: Can I rent out a downtown condo?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been void across BC since November 24, 2022, and the listing checked in any case states rentals allowed. Short-term rentals are a separate municipal/strata question — read the current bylaws on the Form B.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Cedar Court townhouse?

faq.a: Only 1 accessory dwelling unit is permitted per lot under Bylaw 5000: A secondary suite capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the building's habitable floor space, or a coach house, or a garden suite capped at 100 m² — Chilliwack's own figures. Whether a specific duplex parcel qualifies is a parcel read of the bylaw and the lot.
faq.q: Can a downtown duplex also carry a suite or a garden suite?

faq.a: Yes, on form and character: The parcel sits inside the Schedule B3 Downtown Neighbourhood Plan and the D-6 Downtown development permit area — confirm the parcel's designation, DPA set and design-guideline position with the City before valuing any redevelopment potential.
